BIBLIOGRAPHIC RECORD

Walt Whitman (1819–1892).  Prose Works. 1892.

I. Specimen Days

76. The Capitol by Gas-Light

T
O-NIGHT
 I have been wandering awhile in the capitol, which is all lit up. The illuminated rotunda looks fine. I like to stand aside and look a long, long while, up at the dome; it comforts me somehow. The House and Senate were both in session till very late. I look’d in upon them, but only a few moments; they were hard at work on tax and appropriation bills. I wander’d through the long and rich corridors and apartments under the Senate; an old habit of mine, former winters, and now more satisfaction than ever. Not many persons down there, occasionally a fitting figure in the distance.
